title: Tanzanian Bean Stew
community: The everyday bean stew enjoyed nationwide
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Maharage ya Mchuzi — beans simmered in a rich spiced tomato-onion sauce. Tanzania's most essential everyday protein dish — the bean stew that accompanies ugali, rice, and chapati at every meal. Simple, nutritious, and deeply satisfying.
longDesc: Maharage ya Mchuzi (without coconut milk) is Tanzania's everyday bean stew — the tomato-based version eaten from Dodoma to Mwanza, from Arusha to Dar es Salaam. Cheaper than the coconut version and equally nourishing, it is the protein that sustains most of Tanzania daily.
ingredients: 400g dried kidney or borlotti beans — soaked overnight
steps: Cook soaked beans in fresh water 60—75 minutes until tender. Reserve 1 cup liquid.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, tomato paste, spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes until thick.
Simmer 20 minutes until thick and richly flavoured.
chefTips: Completely tender beans before adding to sauce.
Tomato paste deepens the sauce colour and flavour.
Reserve bean liquid — it thickens naturally.
cookingScience: See TZA091 for bean cooking science. The tomato paste's concentrated glutamate (umami) deepens the sauce far beyond what fresh tomatoes alone provide.
sustainabilityTips: Beans are nitrogen-fixing crops — the most sustainable protein available.
culturalNote: Maharage ya Mchuzi is the protein backbone of Tanzania's diet — the bean stew that feeds the nation daily and has sustained Tanzanian communities for generations.
